tor_limits: Timing, usage and content can still link your leases. An agent's own network traffic is not covered.
balances_private: Note balances are private. N is the most notes that could have paid for the lease; fewer may have had enough balance.
includes_unlisted: N includes notes the operator or the team control and did not list.
five_not_safe: With 5 or more external notes, 5 is still not a safe number.
testnet_notes: This is a testnet build. The notes are test notes funded with free testnet USDC, anyone can add them at no cost, and the set is small.
team_pinned_only: team IDs only in this release's pinned list: {ids}
team_operator_only: team IDs only in the operator's list: {ids}
providers_differ: the two RPC providers disagree (set size {a} and {b}); the lower one is used
one_provider: read from one RPC provider only ({why})
operator_list_missing: the operator's team list could not be read; only the pinned list is removed
link_open: The proofs are designed to leave no zero-knowledge link between the deposit and the leases. The leases can still be linked by network address, by timing and usage metadata, or by timing alone while the set is small.
link_left: This note has started to leave, so its leases are now tied to its note ID.
leave_close: A close shows the note ID and the total spend.
leave_clearance: A clearance request shows the operator the note ID and the balance. In the browser it comes from the same address as the leases.
leave_exit: An exit links the last request to the note.
leave_answer: A raise or a defeat ties the answered lease to the note.
leave_sender: The account that sends a close or an exit shows on chain next to the note ID.
leave_exit_purpose: An exit is there to keep the money safe. It does not keep the user private.
reuse_evidence: The operator's status for the request nullifier of the last settled lease is the evidence.
reuse_finalized: finalized: the operator treats this request nullifier as spent.
reuse_reserved: reserved: the operator holds this request nullifier for a lease that has not settled.
reuse_clearance_reserved: clearance_reserved: the operator signed a clearance for this nullifier and treats it as spent.
reuse_unknown: unknown: the operator has no record of this request nullifier.
reuse_other: {status}: a status this page does not know.
reuse_resent: The stored request is inside its 300 seconds, so it was sent to the operator again.
reuse_accepted: The operator did not refuse. It answered the stored request with a lease.
reuse_read_reason: Read the reason. Only a reason about the request nullifier shows the rule. An old proof, a stale root or a missing puzzle is refused for other reasons.
reuse_rule: A refusal is the operator's own rule, backed by its replicated records. The vault does not check it.
reuse_too_old: The stored request is older than 300 seconds, so nothing was sent again. The operator refuses an old proof for its age first, which says nothing about the nullifier rule.
reuse_left: An exit proof has left this device, so nothing is sent again. The status above is all this check shows.
reuse_none: No lease on this note has settled yet, so there is no request nullifier to check.
reuse_no_request: The stored request is not in this copy of the note, so nothing was sent again.
reuse_unreachable: The operator could not be reached ({why}).
who_chain: The chain shows your deposit and, when you close, the note's ID, total spend and payout account.
who_operator: The operator sees your IP address, request times and proofs, not your prompts.
who_entry: The operator's public entry sees your network address and the time of every connection.
who_second: The operator's second machine holds a copy of the lease records, with times rounded to the hour.
who_model: The model in NEAR AI's TEE reads your prompts.
who_near_ai: NEAR AI sees the model, the token counts and the timing of each lease, and can tie the requests of one lease together. It does not see which note the lease belongs to.
who_rpc: RPC providers see your network address with every read and send. The funding step reads the receipt of your own deposit from this browser, so the provider that answers sees your address next to that deposit. Leaving adds reads that name the note ID or the payout account.
who_host: The web host sees your network address and which files you ask for, and it decides which code you get.
who_attest: The attestation services, NEAR AI's attestation endpoint and Phala's PCCS, see the address that asks and the time.
who_certs: Public certificate logs list the operator's host name, which the certificate of its public entry carries. They show that the name exists, not who connects.
who_intents: If the note was funded through Intents, 1Click and the Intents explorer can pair your source wallet with the deposit's commitment and payout account.
